Print all primes till N.approach: Sieve composite multiples starting at p² for every unmarked p. Any composite has a prime factor <=sqrt(n), so it is eventually marked.
Print all primes till N.complexity: O(n log log n) time; O(n) sieve plus output space.
Print all primes till N.trace: 2 marks evens above 2, 3 marks 9,15, then remaining values are prime.
Print all primes till N.pitfalls: n=0/1 returns empty. This uses an array of n+1 entries; huge ranges need segmentation.

Prime factorisation of a Number.problem: Return prime factors with multiplicity for positive n; 1 has an empty factorization.
Prime factorisation of a Number.approach: Repeatedly divide by the smallest divisor. After exhausting smaller factors, the current divisor must be prime if it divides. Any leftover >1 after sqrt(current n) is prime.
Prime factorisation of a Number.complexity: O(sqrt(original n)) worst time; O(log n) output entries.
Prime factorisation of a Number.trace: 360 -> divide 2 three times leaves 45 -> divide 3 twice leaves 5 -> append 5.
Prime factorisation of a Number.pitfalls: Loop bound uses the shrinking n. Reject zero, whose factorization is not finite.

Count primes in range L to R.problem: Count primes in inclusive [l,r] for nonnegative int endpoints. Segment length is limited to ten million to bound memory.
Count primes in range L to R.approach: Sieve primes through sqrt(r), then mark only their multiples inside the segment, starting no earlier than p² so p is not marked composite.
Count primes in range L to R.complexity: O(sqrt(r) log log r + segmentLength*log log r + sqrt(r)) approximate sieve time; O(sqrt(r)+segmentLength) space.
Count primes in range L to R.pitfalls: Exclude 0 and 1 separately. Use long for first multiple and marking positions to avoid endpoint overflow.
